en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammapaccanīyānuloma (4), Dukatikapaṭṭhānapāḷi (3) 21.52.
Mahantaraduka, Sanidassanattika
Dependent on a state that is non-objective, non-visible, and impinging, there arises a state that is non-objective, visible, and impinging by way of root condition … one.
Dependent on a state that is non-objective, non-visible, and impinging, there arises a state that is non-objective, visible, and impinging by way of root condition … one.
(Abbreviated. Under root condition there are three; under predominance condition there are three … pe … under non-disappearance condition there are three.

(For the *anidassana-sappaṭigha* [non-indicative-with-resistance] class, there are three only. Under the root condition (*hetu*), three; under the predominance condition (*adhipati*), three ... pe ... under the mutuality condition (*aññamañña*), one ... pe ... under the non-disappearance condition (*avigata*), three.

Dependent on a state that is not-object-conditioned (*na-ārammaṇa*), not-indicative, and not-resistant (*anidassana-appaṭigha*), there arises a state that is not-object-conditioned, not-indicative, and not-resistant, by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated. Under the root condition, one; under the predominance condition, one ... pe ... under the non-disappearance condition, one.

Dependent on a state that is not-mental (*no-citta*), not-indicative, and resistant (*sappaṭigha*), there arises a state that is not-mental, indicative, and resistant, by way of the root condition ... one.
Dependent on a non-mental state that is non-visible and non-reactive, there arises a non-mental state that is visible and reactive by way of root condition … one. (Abbreviated.
Under root condition there are three; under predominance condition there are three … pe … under non-disappearance condition there are three.
Dependent on a non-mental concomitant state that is non-visible and non-reactive, there arises a non-mental concomitant state that is visible and reactive by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.)
With respect to the root condition, three; with respect to the predominance condition, three …pe… with respect to the non-disappearance condition, three.

Dependent on a state that is not associated with consciousness, is not visible, and is impinging, a state that is dissociated from consciousness, is visible, and is impinging arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated.
With respect to the root condition, three; with respect to the predominance condition, three …pe… with respect to the non-disappearance condition, three.

Dependent on a state that is not conjoined with mind, non-visible, and non-reactive, there arises a state that is conjoined with mind, visible, and reactive, by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. There are three [conditions] under root;
three under predominance …pe… three under non-disappearance.

Dependent on a state that is not mind-originated, non-visible, and non-reactive, there arises a state that is mind-originated, visible, and reactive, by way of root condition. (There are three [conditions] for mind-originated matter alone. Abbreviated.)
With respect to the root condition, there are three; with respect to the predominance condition, there are three ... [and so on] ... with respect to the non-disappearance condition, there are three.

Dependent on a state that is not co-existent with consciousness and is both visible and impinging, there arises a state that is not co-existent with consciousness and is both visible and impinging, by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated. With respect to the root condition, there are three;
with respect to the predominance condition, there are three ... [and so on] ... with respect to the non-disappearance condition, there are three.

Dependent on a state that does not follow the mind, is non-demonstrable, and impinging, there arises a state that does not follow the mind, is demonstrable, and impinging, by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. Under root condition there are three;
under predominance condition there are three ... pe ... under non-disappearance condition there are three.

Dependent on a state that is not conjoined with or produced by the mind, is non-demonstrable, and impinging, there arises a state that is not conjoined with or produced by the mind, is demonstrable, and impinging, by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.)
With respect to the root condition, there are three; with respect to the predominance condition, there are three ... pe ... with respect to the non-disappearance condition, there are three.

Dependent on a state that is not conjoined with, not produced by, and not co-existent with consciousness, and is visible and impinging, there arises a state that is not conjoined with, not produced by, and co-existent with consciousness, and is visible and impinging, by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated. With respect to the root condition, there are three;
with respect to the predominance condition, there are three ... pe ... with respect to the non-disappearance condition, there are three.

Dependent on a state that is not conjoined with mind, not co-arisen with mind, and not accompanying mind, which is visible and impinging, there arises a state that is not conjoined with mind, not co-arisen with mind, and not accompanying mind, which is visible and impinging, by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.
There are three [results] under root, three under predominance …pe… three under non-disappearance.
Dependent on an internal state that is non-visible and non-reacting, an external state that is visible and reacting arises by way of root condition … one.
Dependent on a non-external state that is non-visible and non-reacting, an external state that is visible and reacting arises by way of root condition … one. (Abbreviated.
Under root condition there are three; under predominance condition there are three … pe … under non-disappearance condition there are three.

Dependent on a state that is not acquired by clinging (*anupādāna*), non-manifesting (*asanidassana*), and impinging (*sappaṭigha*), there arises a state that is acquired by clinging (*upādāna*), manifesting (*sanidassana*), and impinging (*sappaṭigha*), by way of root condition (*hetu-paccaya*). (Abbreviated. Under root condition: one;
under predominance condition: one … [and so on] … under non-disappearance condition: one.

Dependent on a state that is not acquired by clinging, non-manifesting, and impinging, there arises a state that is not acquired by clinging, manifesting, and impinging, by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.)
With respect to the root condition, there are three; with respect to the predominance condition, there are three …pe… with respect to the non-disappearance condition, there are three.
